title: Defining the replay sequence
section: A block bootstrap of the history
text:
A block bootstrap of the history
Resampling draws blocks of days and joins them into a new path. Two rules keep the path valid:

Draw days, not symbols, so every symbol’s bars in a block come from the same days and the cross-section keeps its correlation. The helper below draws positions, so every frame must share the same dates in the same order (align real data to a common date index first); it checks this.
Give the path its own timeline. Drawn blocks come out of order and may repeat, while a replay needs time to move forward; the path’s bars are placed on new consecutive business days, and gaps and calendars then follow that timeline.

Prices are rebuilt from the drawn daily returns, so blocks join without jumps.

def bootstrap_path(data, block, rng):
    days = next(iter(data.values())).index
    assert all(f.index.equals(days) for f in data.values()), "align every frame to the same dates"
    n = len(days)
    ratio = {s: (f["close"] / f["close"].shift(1)).to_numpy()[1:] for s, f in data.items()}
    # n prices give n - 1 daily ratios; a block may start at any ratio from 0 to n - 1 - block.
    starts = rng.integers(0, n - block, size=(n - 1) // block)
    picked = np.concatenate([np.arange(a, a + block) for a in starts])
    timeline = pd.bdate_range("2030-01-01", periods=len(picked) + 1)
    path = {}
    for s, f in data.items():
        close = f["close"].iloc[0] * np.concatenate([[1.0], np.cumprod(ratio[s][picked])])
        close = np.round(close, -1)
        path[s] = pd.DataFrame(
            {"open": close, "high": close, "low": close, "close": close, "volume": 1e6},
            index=timeline,
        )
    return path


rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
sharpes = [
    pyatl.backtest(Reversal(), bootstrap_path(data, 20, rng)).sharpe for _ in range(50)
]
low, mid, high = np.quantile(sharpes, [0.05, 0.5, 0.95])
print(f"Sharpe over 50 paths: median {mid:.3f}, 5% {low:.3f}, 95% {high:.3f}")

Sharpe over 50 paths: median -0.004, 5% -0.090, 95% 0.073

title: Defining the replay sequence
section: Feeding a generated sequence in blocks
text:
Feeding a generated sequence in blocks
When a path is generated as the run goes, feed_bars takes each block as columns, in the order you want them replayed.

replay = pyatl.Replay(Reversal(), symbols)
path = bootstrap_path(data, 20, np.random.default_rng(5))
table = pd.concat(path, names=["symbol", "time"]).reset_index()
table["order"] = table["symbol"].map(symbols.index)  # ties follow the replay's symbols
table = table.sort_values(["time", "order"])
for _, block in table.groupby(table["time"].dt.to_period("M")):
    replay.feed_bars(
        block["symbol"].to_numpy(), block["time"].to_numpy(),
        open=block["open"], high=block["high"], low=block["low"],
        close=block["close"], volume=block["volume"],
    )
print(replay.finish().closing_equity)

99760150

title: pyatl
text:
Install
pyatl needs Python 3.12 or newer and an installed algotradelib; see its install guide. Then:
pip install git+https://github.com/algotradelib/pyatl.git
If algotradelib is installed under a prefix CMake does not search, set CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to that prefix. pyatl.algotradelib_version tells which library version a build was made against. NumPy is its only Python dependency; the examples read data with pandas, installed separately (pip install pandas).

title: Get started
text:
A strategy is any object with on_bar(ctx, bar) (one bar at a time) or on_bars(ctx, bars) (every symbol’s bar for a period at once), and optionally on_stop(ctx). ctx.target(symbol, quantity) states how many shares to hold; the order fills at the next bar’s open.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyatl

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
days = pd.bdate_range("2024-01-02", periods=250)
close = np.round(50_000 * np.exp(np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.01, len(days)))), -2)
frame = pd.DataFrame(
    {"open": close, "high": close, "low": close, "close": close, "volume": 1_000_000.0},
    index=days,
)


class Crossover:
    """Holds 100 shares while the 5-day mean is above the 20-day mean."""

    def __init__(self, fast=5, slow=20):
        self.fast, self.slow, self.closes = fast, slow, []

    def on_bar(self, ctx, bar):
        self.closes.append(bar.close)
        if len(self.closes) < self.slow:
            return
        fast = sum(self.closes[-self.fast:]) / self.fast
        slow = sum(self.closes[-self.slow:]) / self.slow
        ctx.target(bar.symbol, 100 if fast > slow else 0)


result = pyatl.backtest(
    Crossover(), {"005930": frame}, commission=0.00015, sell_tax=0.002
)
print(f"{result.bars} bars, {len(result.fills['time'])} fills")
print(f"equity {result.opening_equity} -> {result.closing_equity}")
print(f"total return {result.total_return:.2%}")

250 bars, 10 fills
equity 100000000 -> 99884059
total return -0.12%


Keep the state a strategy needs in plain Python (lists, running sums); a window recomputed with pandas on every bar costs more than the replay itself.

title: Get started
text:
A replay you feed yourself
backtest() replays the bars you give it in time order. A Replay takes them in as many calls as you like, in the order you define, and is finished once.

replay = pyatl.Replay(
    Crossover(), ["005930"], commission=0.00015, sell_tax=0.002
)
for quarter in np.array_split(np.arange(len(frame)), 4):
    replay.feed({"005930": frame.iloc[quarter]})
same = replay.finish()
print(same.closing_equity == result.closing_equity)

True


feed_bars takes one long block (a symbol, a time and the prices per row), which is the fastest way to feed a sequence you generate. Each feed is checked before any of it runs: a symbol’s bars must move forward in time, and no bar may end before the bar fed before it.

title: Measures of your own
Measures of your own
text:
The library’s figures, recomputed
result.equity["period_return"] is the series the library’s Sharpe and Sortino are computed from: each period’s return, computed exactly from decimal equity and rounded to eight places, NaN on the first point and wherever the library has no return (after a bar whose equity could not be valued, or after equity at or below zero). For a run like this one, a measure computed from it matches the library’s; one computed from the floating-point equity levels agrees to about four significant digits. If equity was at or below zero before the last point, the library reports no Sharpe or Sortino at all, while the remaining returns would still give a number: check np.isnan(result.sharpe) before comparing.

equity = result.equity["equity"]
returns = result.equity["period_return"]
valid = returns[~np.isnan(returns)]
from_levels = equity[1:] / equity[:-1] - 1
peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
print(f"total return  library {result.total_return:.10f}  numpy {equity[-1] / equity[0] - 1:.10f}")
print(f"max drawdown  library {result.max_drawdown:.10f}  numpy {((peak - equity) / peak).max():.10f}")
print(f"sharpe        library {result.sharpe:.10f}  from period_return {valid.mean() / valid.std(ddof=1):.10f}")
print(f"              from the levels instead {from_levels.mean() / from_levels.std(ddof=1):.10f}")

total return  library -0.0019134200  numpy -0.0019134200
max drawdown  library 0.0092213438  numpy 0.0092213438
sharpe        library -0.0153188045  from period_return -0.0153188045
              from the levels instead -0.0153198587


Check result.unvalued_bars == 0 first: a bar whose equity could not be valued has no point in the curve, and a return computed between two exported points would span it.

section: Measures the library does not report
text:
Measures the library does not report

years = (result.equity["time"][-1] - result.equity["time"][0]) / (365.25 * 86400e9)
cagr = (equity[-1] / equity[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1
var_95 = -np.quantile(valid, 0.05)
fills = pd.DataFrame(result.fills)
trades = fills.groupby("side")["quantity"].sum()
print(f"CAGR {cagr:.2%}, one-day VaR(95%) {var_95:.2%}")
print(f"shares bought {trades.get('buy', 0):.0f}")

One backtest that you feed yourself, in as many steps as you like, then finish once.
backtest() is a Replay fed once. Use a Replay when the sequence of bars is yours to define: a resampled path, a rolling window, bars generated as the run goes. The bars still run through the C++ engine one at a time; in our measurements, feeding a sequence in blocks took no longer than one backtest() call over the same bars.

Every feed is checked whole before its first bar reaches the engine: each symbol’s bars must come later than its previous one, and no bar may end before the bar fed before it. title: Replay
text: Every feed is checked whole before its first bar reaches the engine: each symbol’s bars must come later than its previous one, and no bar may end before the bar fed before it. A refused feed raises ValueError and changes nothing. An exception raised by the strategy ends the replay: later calls raise RuntimeError. A strategy handler may not feed or finish its own replay.

title: BacktestResult
text:
BacktestResult(
    bars,
    fills,
    equity,
    opening_equity,
    closing_equity,
    halted,
    total_return,
    sharpe,
    annualized_sharpe,
    max_drawdown,
    sortino,
    turnover,
    commission_paid,
    tax_paid,
    slippage_paid,
    rejected,
    refused,
    unfilled,
    gaps,
    unvalued_bars,
    lowest_cash,
    aborted,
    overdrawn_bars,
    unchecked_fill_causality,
)
What one replay produced.
fills, equity, rejected and refused are dicts of columns (pandas.DataFrame(result.fills) makes a table). Times are ns since the epoch (UTC). halted says why the replay stopped early, if it did; the figures then cover only what ran. Figures are NaN where the library has none.










Name
Type
Description




bars
int
Bars replayed.


fills
dict of str to array
One row per fill: time, symbol, side (“buy” or “sell”), quantity, price (slippage included), commission, tax (sale tax, KRW) and slippage (the price per share given up to slippage, already in price).


equity
dict of str to array
The equity curve: time, equity, and period_return, the library’s return since the previous point (rounded to eight places), the series its Sharpe and Sortino are computed from. A return is NaN on the first point, after an unvalued bar, after a point with equity at or below zero, and where the exact arithmetic fails; if equity was at or below zero before the last point, the library reports no Sharpe or Sortino at all.


opening_equity, closing_equity
str
Equity at the first and last point, as exact decimal text; empty when the curve has no point.


halted
str or None
Why the replay stopped early, or None.


total_return, max_drawdown
float
The return over the run and the largest fall from a peak, as fractions (0.05 is 5 %).


sharpe, sortino
float
Per period of the equity curve (one bar’s interval), not annualized.


annualized_sharpe
float
sharpe scaled to a year of KRX trading days.


turnover
float
Everything traded (buys and sells, quantity x price) divided by the opening equity, over the whole run.


commission_paid, tax_paid, slippage_paid
float
Costs over the run, KRW; NaN where the library cannot state a total.


rejected
dict of str to list
Targets the runner could not turn into an order: symbol and reason (the library’s name).


refused
dict of str to list or array
Orders the risk guard refused: symbol and reason (lists; the reason is the library’s name), and, as arrays, the limit exceeded and the value attempted, in the reason’s own unit (shares for quantity_not_sellable), NaN where the reason has none.


unfilled
int
Orders still waiting when the replay ended.


gaps
int
Bars that did not follow the bar before them; nothing is interpolated across a gap.


unvalued_bars
int
Bars at which the equity could not be valued exactly (a total too large for an exact decimal); such a bar has no point in equity. The library’s own figures leave the next period’s return out; a return computed between two exported points would span the missing bar. Check it is 0 before computing measures from equity per period.


lowest_cash
float
The lowest cash (KRW) an execution left, if an execution took cash below zero; NaN otherwise, which includes a run that started below zero and executed nothing.


aborted
int
Orders cleared when the replay halted, apart from unfilled.


overdrawn_bars
int
Input bars that ended with cash below zero (with several symbols, one per symbol’s bar).


unchecked_fill_causality
int
Decisions to fill an order against a bar that the engine could not check were made before that bar (for example with weekly, monthly or yearly bars stamped at their close). Counted when the order is matched to the bar, before it is priced, so it is not a count of fills.
